name: Bodrum
tagline: Whitewashed Aegean harbour under a crusader castle
summary: A white harbour town on a peninsula of coves and villages. See the castle and the old town in a day, then spend the rest on a boat, a beach or dinner by the water in Gümüşlük.
seasonNote: July and August are hot, crowded and the most expensive; from November to April much of the peninsula shuts.
arrival: Milas-Bodrum airport is 35 km away; the Havaş bus takes about 45 minutes. Summer ferries run to Kos in 45 minutes.
gettingAround: Dolmuş minibuses fan out from the central station to every village on the peninsula; the old town is on foot.
cashTip: Cards are accepted widely; carry lira for dolmuş fares and beach vendors.
foodTip: Order grilled sea bream or bass, Aegean herb meze, stuffed courgette flowers and çökertme kebabı.
buyTip: Handmade leather sandals are a Bodrum tradition; the Tuesday textile market is the big one.
baseArea: Bodrum town for sights and nightlife; Bitez or Gümüşlük for quiet

connections.note: Direct buses in summer; otherwise change in Söke.

items.name: Bodrum Castle
items.summary: A 15th-century castle of the Knights of St. John that houses the Museum of Underwater Archaeology.
items.expect: Many steps and towers; some halls close for restoration.
items.tip: Do not miss the Uluburun Bronze Age shipwreck hall.

items.name: Gümüşlük
items.summary: A fishing village on the site of ancient Myndos, with tables set at the water's edge.
items.expect: No new building is allowed, so it stays low-key; busy for sunset.
items.tip: Wade across the sunken causeway to Rabbit Island, then stay for fish.
